newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi says sanctions ministers to visit.
newsitem.headline: Burundi says sanctions ministers to visit.

text.p: Burundi's government said on Thursday that three ministers from East African states that imposed sanctions on the landlocked country would stage a delayed visit to the capital, Bujumbura on Friday.
"Three East African ministers will come tomorrow (Friday), arriving at around 9 am (0700 GMT)," according to a foreign ministry statement.

There was no confirmation of the visit from outside Burundi, but a senior U.N. official and government officials said foreign ministers from Tanzania, Uganda and Zaire were due in Burundi on Friday morning.

A visit by East African ministers could break a deadlock over sanctions after Burundi's military regime and regional states imposed contradictory conditions for the ending of an economic and transport embargo.
The ministers cancelled a planned visit on Wednesday in response to an announcement by Burundi's regime that it would not start unconditional talks with Hutu rebels until the blockade was lifted.

Regional states including Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda first imposed economic and transport sanctions on the landlocked country six days after retired major Pierre Buyoya took power in a military coup on July 25.
Earlier this month the states decided to maintain the blockade, setting a one month deadline for the start of unconditional all-party negotiations.
